comments.text_zh: John Baez 的博客有一个关于文明如何崩溃的系列，先看阿纳萨齐人，然后讲如何用基于主体的建模来模拟，也通过微分方程来研究一般性的崩溃：[链接] [链接] [链接] [链接] James Burke 是科学史学家和 BBC 纪录片制作人，在他探讨创新本质的系列片《Connections》第一集中，他谈到我们复杂的基建设施可能有多脆弱，并且和这篇文章很像，他指出一旦我们“离开技术的子宫”，个人主义的生存技能将毫无用处。[视频] 在他后来的系列《After the Warming》中——这部 1988 年的纪录片设想如果我们对气候变化不作为，2050 年会是什么样子（片中预测了难民危机、战争、飓风、大规模洪水）——并回溯了数千年来气候如何塑造文明的兴衰，从冰河时代到纳巴泰人，再到今天乃至更远的未来。它把大多数事情都说对了，准得吓人，唯一明显的例外是没预见到 1991 年日本经济泡沫破裂。[链接] [链接]
comments.text: John Baez's blog has a series on how civilizations collapse, first looking at the Anasazi, and then how one might model it using agent-based modeling and also looking at general collapse through differential equations: [LINK] [LINK] [LINK] [LINK] James Burke is a science historian and BBC documentarian, and in his first episode of "Connections" a series on the nature of innovation, he talks about how fragile our complex infrastructure can be, and, much like this article, how hopeless individualist survival skills would be once we "leave our technological womb". [VIDEO] In his later series, After the Warming, a 1988 documentary which imagines what it would look like in 2050 if we failed to act on climate change (in which it predicted refugee crises, wars, hurricanes, mass flooding), and looks back on thousands of years of climate shaping civilizational rise and collapse, from the Ice Age to the Nabataeans to today and beyond. It gets most things scarily right, with the notable exception of failing to see Japanese economic bubble popping in 1991. [LINK] [LINK]

comments.text_zh: > "我们不会停止生产足够的粮食来养活美国所有人" 大萧条呢？魏玛共和国恶性通胀呢？我相信现代也有例子。也许食物和其他产品很充足，但如果负责加工并把它们运到所需之处的社会和经济结构崩溃了，那些食物就跟在月球背面差不多。甚至连生产那些食物都成问题。如今现代生产依赖机械和电子系统，连农业也是如此。没有替换零件和消耗品供应，一切都会迅速停摆。我们在最近的 COVID-19 短缺中看到了一个例子；来自海外的包装和其他消耗品短缺，阻碍了国内产品的生产，即使产品的实际内容物仍然可得。今天一切都是相互关联的。一切。看看 James Burke 那部出色纪录片《Connections》的第一集，就能了解当这种联系崩溃时会发生什么：[VIDEO]
comments.text: > " we're not going to stop being able to produce enough food to feed everyone in the US " The Great Depression? Hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic? I'm sure there are modern examples as well. There may be a plentitude of food and other products but if the societal and economic structures that process it and get it to where it needs to be collapse, that food might as well be on the far side of the moon. And even producing that food is questionable. Modern production is reliant on mechanical and electronic systems nowadays, even farming. Without replacement parts and consumable supplies, everything rapidly grinds to a halt. We saw an example of this in the recent COVID-19 shortages; lack of packaging and other consumables from overseas blocked domestic production of products even when the actual content of the product was still available. Everything is interlinked today. Everything. Watch episode one of James Burke's excellent documentary "Connections" to get an idea of what occurs when that breaks down: [VIDEO]

comments.text: I wouldn't be surprised if it is spreading this way. If not already, then certainly in future. Having said that, a steady stream of supplies is what will allow everyone else to stay holed-up. If you can't get the supplies you need to get through the ordeal then you'll start to see individuals go out on far-and-wide "hunting trips" to find those supplies (at best) or you'll start to see societal breakdowns which will give Covid-19 a run for its money on lives and damages. It may be trucks delivering electrical equipment to keep refrigeration running, to keep other trucks, moving, etc. Modern life depends on surprisingly deep connections. [VIDEO]

Think of how even this discussion about TP reveals a large scale bifurcation of how a singular, simple product is produced and supplied. How much does the essential economy depend on the non-essential economy? For example, one client made higher end bicycle parts and the other made lab equipment for bio-tech applications. comments.story_title: How prepared are we for the next giant solar flare?
comments.text_zh: 一家公司不为灾难做准备，其成本被极大地外部化了，导致风险等式失衡，这代表着一种市场失灵。在德州，这种市场失灵的代价可以用本可避免的死亡人数来衡量，而私营能源公司在管理风险时根本无需为其中任何一项负责。如果太阳耀斑导致全国电力中断数月，代价可能是现代文明的崩溃。[VIDEO]
comments.text: The cost of a company not preparing for a catastrophe is hugely externalized, resulting in a lopsided risk equation that represents a market failure. In texas, the cost of that market failure can be measured in preventable deaths, none of which private energy companies needed to account for when managing risk. In the event of a solar flare knocking out national power for months, the cost could be the collapse of modern civilization. [VIDEO]
